newsitem.title: CANADA: CAW sees settlement with Chrysler Canada.
newsitem.headline: CAW sees settlement with Chrysler Canada.

text.p: Canadian Auto Workers union president Buzz Hargrove said on Tuesday that he expects to reach a contract agreement with Chrysler Corp's Canadian unit.
"Even if we cannot resolve this today, it's clear over the next few days we will have a settlement that sets a new standard for working people throughout the country," Hargrove told reporters.
He added that time was short ahead of tonight's midnight strike deadline, which he has declined to consider extending.
"We are not going to lift the deadline," Hargrove said.
Talks broke open late Monday after the CAW and Chrysler Canada reached a deal on the key issue of outsourcing.
The union had halted talks Monday afternoon except on the outsourcing issue to try to force a deal. The CAW represents 12,600 Chrysler Canada workers.
Company officials said today they were worried there might not be enough time to resolve other issues since negotiators lost five hours to the halt on Monday.
"We're certainly concerned about the little time remaining," said Chrysler Canada spokesman Walt McCall. "We think it's attainable, but it's going to be tough."

Company and union officials said the key issues left to resolve were contained in the economic package. The CAW said it was concerned about the company's demands for user fees and co-payments to the health care plan, as well as wages.
"Today we turn our full attention the economic package," McCall told Reuters.
